reasons: Status is correctly 'deviation' rather than 'compliant': the finding itself concedes IBM's Section 8.1 IP indemnity sits at the fallback and leaves it untouched, and flags only the separate customer-side limb. Section 8.2(a)(3) makes Customer indemnify IBM for any Services Recipient claim 'related, directly or indirectly, to the Services', which is precisely the 'one-way Customer indemnity for Vendor's services' the rule treats as walk-away, and it fails the preferred requirement that Customer's indemnity be limited to Customer content and Customer's breach of law. Section 8.2(c)'s carve-back only for IBM's bad faith/wilful misconduct/gross negligence/breach leaves ordinary-negligence and service-defect exposure with us, so the deviation is material and not double-flagged elsewhere.

Redline is actionable, directionally correct and minimal in scope: it edits only the offending sub-clause (p0101), replacing the 'directly or indirectly related to the Services' trigger with 'arises out of Content or Customer's breach of applicable law, and not out of IBM's performance of the Services', which tracks the playbook's preferred customer-indemnity scope. It preserves the enumerated-list grammar of 8.2(a) and does not disturb the acceptable Vendor IP indemnity, exclusions or remedies.

Deterministic signals are heuristic and do not undermine the substance: the 'vendor indemnity for IP infringement present' regex fails only because IBM's indemnity in p0089 is phrased around 'Materials or Base Components' infringing a party's 'patent, trademark, copyright, or trade secret' rather than the pattern wording, and the 0.59 changed-character ratio is expected when an indemnity trigger must be rewritten wholesale.

Comment is accurate, correctly attributes the acceptable status of Section 8.1, states what changed and why, cites the playbook position, uses the [Playbook] prefix and first-person plural, and does not lecture. Minor residual note only: 'Content' is assumed to be a defined term in the agreement (not shown in resolved definitions) - confirm the capitalised term exists, otherwise substitute 'Customer's content or data'.
